data.hypothesis: The measured warp-per-target kernel is a strong base. Processing two consecutive source indices per lane per loop trip may reduce loop-control overhead and expose independent interaction work to the compiler. The source order and arithmetic expression for each lane remain unchanged; correctness and performance still require controller validation.

memory_lessons.applicability: Evidence is from this campaign and its search measurements; it does not establish a general performance rule.
memory_lessons.claim: The correct warp-per-target candidate measured 0.00014804925230338682 seconds, faster than the correct shared-memory candidate at 0.0009205335376977983 seconds and the baseline at 0.0018433244440074987 seconds.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this two-source loop-unroll variant with the official correctness checks and timing protocol.

data.notes: Retain the measured warp mapping and launch configuration (256 threads, 8 items per block, 0 shared bytes). The unrolled loop preserves each lane's increasing source order, skips self-interaction (including the extreme-mass isolated case), and keeps tail and overflow guards. This candidate has not been compiled, checked, or measured in this integration turn; do not infer a speedup before controller results.
transformations: Retained T2's warp-per-target source-axis mapping, warp reductions, and 256-thread/8-items-per-block configuration.
Unrolled each lane's source loop by two interactions per trip while preserving each lane's increasing source order, self-interaction skip, tail handling, and overflow-safe index updates.
